lesson.title: Assess representation, context and missing data
lesson.summary: Assess data suitability for people and deployment context.

prerequisites.reason: Quality applies to the appropriate datasets.

blocks: **Representation** means the data adequately reflects relevant people or groups for the intended purpose. Sets must be relevant, sufficiently representative and, to the best extent possible, error-free and complete.
Appropriate statistical properties may be met within individual sets or their combination. Neither “perfect data always” nor “large data is enough” states the statutory standard.

**Deployment-context fit** asks whether data reflects relevant geographical, contextual, behavioural and functional settings. Northbridge’s past office-role applicants do not automatically validate a new apprenticeship use in another labour market.
Record which differences matter to the intended purpose. Size does not answer whether language, application forms or job types have changed.
**Data-gap remediation** identifies relevant missing or weak data that prevents compliance and how to address it. Include needed availability, quantity and suitability in the assessment.

For an unsupported group or context, possible responses include obtaining suitable data, changing the permitted scope or holding that use pending evidence. These are assessor choices; the statute does not prescribe one universal collection method.
Case: a very large set excludes a group relevant to the intended deployment. An overall performance claim cannot by itself establish suitability for that group.
The file should connect purpose, people, context, gaps, measures and resulting evidence. An unresolved gap stays a limitation or gate rather than disappearing into the average.

questions.prompt: Northbridge’s large dataset excludes a relevant applicant group. Does size establish sufficient representation?

options.blocks: No; assess relevant representation and statistical properties
options.reason: Purpose and relevant groups determine suitability.
Large sets can still omit relevant groups.

options.blocks: Only absolutely perfect sets satisfy the law
options.reason: The text uses “to the best extent possible” for errors and completeness.
